    AI Mode reply for zenhub alternatives

    Top alternatives to Zenhub depend on whether you want to stay inside GitHub or move to a standalone project management tool. 
    Staying Inside GitHub
    • GitHub Projects: The most native choice if your team already lives on GitHub. It supports iteration planning, custom fields, and built-in insight charts without extra subscription fees. However, it is unopinionated and restricts you to managing a single repository at a time rather than multi-repo workspaces. 
    Standalone Scrum & Agile Tools
    • Linear: Built specifically for engineering teams that value speed. It offers lightning-fast issue triage, keyboard-first navigation, cycles (sprints), and clean roadmaps, though it does not deeply mirror GitHub's exact issue-first structure. 
    • Jira: A heavy-duty, enterprise-scale choice for complex workflows, custom tracking, and detailed scrum or kanban ceremonies. It includes a free tier for up to 10 users. 
    • Shortcut: A developer-focused tool with native iteration planning that bridges the gap between engineering workflows and general product tracking. It also features a free tier for up to 10 users. 
    • Scrumpy: Designed specifically for teams migrating away from GitHub-coupled tracking. It offers free, unlimited view-only seats for non-engineers (like designers, clients, or product owners) who do not need a GitHub account. 
    Cross-Functional & All-in-One Workspaces
    • ClickUp: A converged workspace that unifies tasks, docs, goals, and chat. It is great for cross-functional teams where marketing, design, and engineering need to collaborate in one place. 
    • Asana: Ideal for cross-team roadmaps, high-level milestone tracking, and connecting technical work with broader company goals. 
    See how Zenhub compares directly with native GitHub Projects when managing multi-repository workflows:
